adds.title: North West trans community desperate for hormone replacement services
adds.summary: The trans community in North West province cannot access hormone replacement therapy (HRT) at any public health facility in the province and residents are forced to travel sometimes hundreds of kilometres to Soweto in Gauteng to get it, MambaOnline reported on 21 February 2023. The North West Department of Health confirmed it has no facilities providing HRT for transgender people, in its response to a complaint lodged by Action for Social Justice International with the SA Human Rights Commission. Documents the province-level absence of trans-specific healthcare that a trans visitor reliant on prescribed HRT would confront on the ground.

adds.title: Lesbian pupil banned from school in North West
adds.summary: MambaOnline (23 March 2016, citing the Taung Daily News) reported that 18-year-old lesbian Zinzi Manini Molema of Maphoitsile village, North West, was barred from attending school for refusing to wear a skirt; the principal sent her home saying she must wear a skirt 'since I was a girl', and she stayed home for three weeks without attending any classes. Records a North West institution enforcing a gendered dress code against a gender-nonconforming pupil, illustrating the province's socially conservative enforcement climate.

adds.title: New Report on LGBT Community in North West
adds.summary: A report entitled 'Same-sex sexuality in North-West province', released in October 2010, presented the results of a survey conducted under the auspices of the UNISA Centre for Applied Psychology during 2009 and 2010, with OUT LGBT Well-being, OUT North-West and Gay Umbrella collaborating; it surveyed 319 LGBT people from a largely rural background in one of the country's poorest and most under-populated provinces, asking about openness about same-sex sexuality, how LGBT persons perceive their environment, and sexual abuse and discrimination. Provides the province-level 2010 survey behind this record's data-presence signal for North West.

adds.title: Transgender Woman in Brutal Hate Crime Attack in Tshwane Tavern
adds.summary: Aobakwe Mahlobo, a 23-year-old transgender woman originally from Soshanguve and living in Winterveld (both in Tshwane, Gauteng), was assaulted at a local tavern at about 1:30 am on 26 December 2024 after a man began saying gay and lesbian people 'don't deserve to live'; he smashed a bottle into her face as she lit a cigarette, saying 'I told you I'm gonna kill you', leaving deep cuts to her mouth, lips, nose, cheek and forehead that were stitched after treatment at Kgabo Clinic. She opened an assault case at Dube Police Station, which MambaOnline (6 January 2025) reported had shown no progress. The province's most recent documented trans-specific hate incident on record.

adds.title: Media Statement: National Preventive Mechanism welcomes the High Court ruling affirming the rights of transgender persons in correctional facilities
adds.summary: The SA Human Rights Commission's National Preventive Mechanism (14 November 2025) welcomed the judgment of the Gauteng Division of the High Court, Johannesburg, in Nthabiseng Beverly Mokoena v Head of Johannesburg Correctional Centre and Others (Case No. 2024/070075), delivered on 10 November 2025. The court found the Department of Correctional Services engaged in unfair discrimination and harassment of the transgender inmate by refusing to allow her to express her gender identity and denying her prescribed gender-affirming hormone therapy, and held that the constitutional right to adequate medical treatment includes gender-affirming hormonal therapy at state expense, ordering the DCS to implement accommodations and enforce its own SOPs. Demonstrates an operational Gauteng court remedy, under PEPUDA, for discrimination against a trans person.

adds.title: Trans Woman Stands Her Ground After Stadium Bathroom Incident in Cape Town
adds.summary: Taswald Ruiters, a transgender woman from Eerste River, Cape Town, was threatened with removal from the Green Point Athletic Stadium on 19 February 2025 after using the women's bathroom; a security guard told her 'Look at you, you're a man', ordered her to use the men's bathroom and claimed he had the final say, and police called four times never arrived in nearly three hours, MambaOnline reported on 28 February 2025. The stadium is a public facility operated by the City of Cape Town, with the venue rented on the day by Western Province Athletics, which was responsible for the security services. Records the enforcement-and-response gap a visibly trans visitor can meet in the province's best-resourced metro, without any provincial rule restricting bathroom use by trans people.
